items.title: D. Mass. stays and preliminarily enjoins SEVP August 2026 CPT broadcasts
items.summary: On 17 November 2026, Judge Julia E. Kobick (D. Mass.) granted plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction and stay of agency action in Association of American Universities v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-14520-JEK (ECF 36, 24-page signed memorandum). A nationwide stay under APA § 705 provides that SEVP’s Broadcast Messages of 12 August 2026 and 24 August 2026 (previously tracked as BCM 2608-01/02), which limited curricular practical training to training required of all students in a degree program and excluded elective for-credit internships, “may not be enforced or applied pending judicial review.” A party-specific preliminary injunction under Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a) also enjoins defendants from carrying out that interpretation of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(f)(10)(i) as to the plaintiff associations and each of their members, including employees and students, both prospectively and as to pre-broadcast conduct and approvals. The court found a likelihood of success on the APA arbitrary-and-capricious claim (unexplained change from the post-1991 treatment of elective for-credit CPT, and failure to consider reliance interests), irreparable harm, and favorable equities; it did not reach other APA claims. The court declined to order rescission of adverse actions already taken or written notice to all SEVP-certified institutions. This is preliminary relief, not a final judgment; no notice of appeal or stay of this order was visible on CourtListener this morning (last known filing 17 November 2026; last updated 17 November 2026, 10:50 a.m. ET). ICE SEVIS / Study in the States pages were not yet updated. Not legal advice.
items.slate_impact: Material for the entire Fall 2027 CS/MBA/MSF international slate, especially internship-heavy paths. Elective for-credit internships, co-ops, and practicums were the category the August broadcasts treated as ineligible for CPT. Call out MSF separately: many MSF/MFE/quant internships are elective or for-credit rather than required of every student in the degree. The § 705 stay is nationwide; the Rule 65 injunction covers plaintiff-association members and their students. Already-denied fall CPT is not automatically restored. Subject to appeal. Not school-specific as a new ISSS policy, though the opinion recites Fall 2026 operational harm at Columbia, Cornell, Dartmouth, Vanderbilt, and WashU.

items.title: D. Mass. vacates DHS fixed-admission / end-of-duration-of-status final rule
items.summary: On 16 November 2026, Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV (D. Mass.) granted plaintiffs’ motion for summary judgment and denied defendants’ in Presidents’ Alliance v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-13799 (ECF 73). The court VACATED the 17 July 2026 Final Rule (91 Fed. Reg. 44976, FR Doc. 2026-14439) under APA § 706 and directed entry of final judgment; ECF 74 dismisses the case (terminated 16 November 2026). Duration of status remains the governing framework unless a higher court stays or reverses the judgment or DHS issues a new rule. 18 November 2026 scan update: no new district-court filing and no stay of the vacatur (CL last known filing still 16 November 2026; last updated 17 November 2026, 11:21 a.m. ET). The First Circuit appeal of the September 14 PI (No. 26-2112) is now confirmed, on CourtListener, to have been placed in abeyance on 13 November 2026: Appellate Judge Lara E. Montecalvo granted the government’s assented-to motion, vacated the briefing schedule, and directed a status report at the end of thirty days (CL last known filing 13 November 2026; last updated 17 November 2026, 6:25 a.m. ET). No separate appeal or stay of the final judgment was visible. ICE SEVIS / Study in the States pages still showed the July 17 final-rule banner. Not legal advice.
items.slate_impact: Unchanged merits posture versus the 17 November ship: a final vacatur, with duration of status remaining the framework unless stayed or reversed. The new fact is only that the pending First Circuit PI appeal (26-2112) is in a 30-day abeyance as of 13 November 2026, with a status report due at the end of that period. MSF and same- or lower-level / joint-degree pathways remain in scope of the district court’s academic-mobility holding. Not school-specific.
